podcast.body: This album is named after a somewhat dated, brutalist-architecture mall in downtown Hamilton, which for the band symbolized the city's core and its inspiring "fight." The album reflects the city's atmosphere before widespread gentrification, capturing stories that might take place there, such as the one in the song "Abigail." "It felt... I don't know. It was the core of Hamilton and I think for us, there was a part of it that we found to be really like inspiring about Hamilton, sort of like the fight in the city and around that time as well in 2008, I feel like the city was... There was like this light in the distance that we could sort of see that it was changing, that there was this creative community."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This debut album was recorded quickly, in roughly two weeks, due to budget constraints, with bed tracks recorded in five days and overdubs done in a cheap studio. It was described as a concise encapsulation of four years of live songs, refined through performance, and characterized by a loud, fast rock sound with edgy guitars and super loud drums, reflecting a less open approach to diverse influences at the time. "We recorded Jackson Square in basically, you know, two weeks or a little bit over two weeks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
